title: Alcaraz wins in three sets as Kartal marks her WTA return
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz and Sonay Kartal recorded victories as they returned to tour tennis after injury breaks. Their matches took place at different tournaments, with Alcaraz competing in Japan and Kartal in China.

Defending Japan Open champion Alcaraz defeated Alex Michelsen 7-6 (7-1) 4-6 6-1. He needed a tie-break to win the first set, lost the second, then won the deciding set. In tennis, a tie-break is a shorter scoring contest used when a set is level in games.

The Spanish world number three had been sidelined for just over five months by a wrist injury. He returned at the US Open, reaching the quarter-finals before this appearance on the ATP Tour. The ATP Tour is the main men's professional tennis circuit.

His serve was inconsistent against Michelsen. He produced five aces, which the receiver could not touch, but also five double faults. A double fault happens when a player misses both service attempts and loses the point.

At the China Open in Beijing, Britain's Kartal beat Spain's Andrea Lazaro Garcia 6-2 6-3. The 24-year-old injured her lower back at Indian Wells in March and had been away from the WTA Tour for almost six months. The WTA Tour is the main women's professional tennis circuit.

Kartal first returned to competition at the Billie Jean King Cup on September 22, narrowly losing to Marie Bouzkova. She then won in Beijing. Ranked 129th in the world, she will next face Chinese 31st seed Wang Xinyu as she tries to move back up the rankings.
why_it_matters: The results show both players competing successfully on tour after injury breaks. Kartal's next match continues her attempt to climb the rankings.
